entry.title: Screen Reader Navigation of Data Dashboards: A Study with Blind Analysts
entry.summary: Interactive dashboards have become the default way organisations share data, yet navigating them with a screen reader remains challenging. We interviewed 18 blind and low-vision analysts about their daily work. Participants described a lack of structural cues: charts are announced as single images, filters reset focus, and existing tools fail to expose relationships between linked views. We distil six design requirements and present a prototype that exposes dashboard structure as a navigable tree.

entry.title: Why Do Code Review Bots Get Ignored?
entry.summary: Automated review bots post thousands of comments on pull requests every day. We mined 40,000 bot comments across 300 open-source projects and found that maintainers act on fewer than one in ten. Through follow-up interviews we find that bots fail to explain why a change matters and that their suggestions arrive after a human has already approved the change. We discuss timing, tone, and evidence as levers for bot designers.

entry.title: A Larger Pretraining Corpus for Low-Resource Machine Translation
entry.summary: We release a parallel corpus of 12 million sentence pairs covering 40 language pairs. Models pretrained on the corpus improve BLEU by 2.1 points on average over the previous best public baseline. We describe the collection pipeline, deduplication, and quality scoring, and we release all code and model checkpoints under a permissive licence so that others can build on the results.

entry.title: Detecting Misinformation in Community Health Forums
entry.summary: This paper has been withdrawn by the authors due to an error in the evaluation protocol. The lack of a held-out test split means the reported numbers overstate performance; a corrected version will be submitted as a new article once the experiments have been rerun on a properly separated dataset with independent annotators.

entry.title: Erratum: Benchmarking Sign Language Recognition in the Wild
entry.summary: This erratum corrects Table 3 of our earlier article, in which the accuracy of the pose-only baseline was reported for the wrong split. The corrected figures do not change our conclusions: existing methods struggle with fingerspelling, and the gap between laboratory and in-the-wild footage is still large for every model we evaluated.

entry.title: Online Forms for Public Services: Where Citizens Give Up
entry.summary: Many government services are now available only online. Using clickstream logs from a municipal benefits portal, we locate the steps where applicants abandon their forms. Little is known about why abandonment concentrates on identity checks; we find that applicants struggle to upload documents from phones, a barrier to access for residents without a computer.

entry.title: Federated Learning for Hospital Readmission Prediction
entry.summary: Hospitals cannot share patient records, which limits the data available to readmission models. We propose a federated optimiser with adaptive client weighting and prove it converges under non-IID data. Existing methods struggle with heterogeneous clients; ours improves AUROC by 3 points across five simulated hospital networks while keeping communication costs comparable to the strongest federated baselines.

entry.title: TriageNet: Attention-Based Prioritisation of Emergency Calls
entry.summary: Emergency response centres receive more calls than dispatchers can handle during disasters. Manual triage is time-consuming and error-prone. We introduce TriageNet, a hierarchical attention architecture over call transcripts, and show it outperforms transformer baselines on a dataset of 20,000 annotated calls from two regional centres, with the largest gains on calls that mention multiple casualties.

entry.title: On the Fairness of Allocating Tutors to Students
entry.summary: Schools often lack enough tutors for every student who needs one. We model tutor allocation as a matching problem and characterise when envy-free allocations exist. We give a polynomial algorithm for the two-subject case, show the general case is NP-hard, and leave approximation guarantees for more than three subjects as an open problem for future theoretical work on matching under capacity constraints.

entry.title: A Dataset of Annotated Lesson Plans from Secondary Schools
entry.summary: We release 12,000 lesson plans written by secondary-school teachers in four countries, annotated with learning objectives, activities, and assessment types. We describe the collection and annotation process, report inter-annotator agreement, and provide baseline classifiers for objective tagging. The dataset and annotation guidelines are available under an open licence for teachers and researchers to reuse.

entry.title: Annotation Tools for Wildlife Camera Traps Remain Error-Prone
entry.summary: Conservation groups label millions of camera-trap images by hand. This process is time-consuming and error-prone, and existing tools fail to support the review workflows that volunteers actually use. We study three projects and propose a triage interface that surfaces likely-empty frames first and lets experts audit volunteer labels in bulk.
